title: Continuous On-Chain Monitoring: Temporal Drift + Finding Lifecycle (V2.9)
description: Reference shapes for scripts/monitor_diff.py's two output modes (docs/decisiones.md D-063). This script NEVER makes a network call, NEVER stores snapshot/scan history, NEVER alerts, and NEVER generates a timestamp itself - snapshotTimestamp is always caller-supplied. It reuses compare_bytecode.py's normalize_hex/strip_cbor_metadata/byte_divergence_profile and diff_reports.py's diff_reports()/stableKey UNCHANGED. All results are structural facts, never automatic security verdicts.

coverageStatus.description: M3. A WINDOW/coverage status ONLY - a distinct vocabulary from compare_bytecode.py's five bytecode verdicts (MATCH/MISMATCH/UNAVAILABLE/INCOMPLETE/UNRESOLVED), which this script never touches or adds to.

identicalToLastSnapshot.description: M3 idempotency: true when the two snapshots' comparison-relevant content hashes match (excluding snapshotTimestamp).

temporalDrift.description: M1. Output of compute_temporal_snapshot_drift(). snapshot1 is assumed earlier, snapshot2 later, by argument order alone - never inferred from timestamp values. Identity is (chainId, address) - BOTH must resolve and match exactly (D-064) or the function raises before any comparison is attempted; chainId is the canonical numeric form resolved via chains.py - a network name/alias is never identity by itself.

chainId.description: D-064. Canonical numeric chainId shared by both snapshots.

flagChanges.description: Only entries where the field actually changed. verified/hasCode are always compared; adminAddress/ownerAddress are compared ONLY when both snapshots supply a usable value - never guessed.

divergenceProfile.description: MISMATCH only. Reused verbatim from compare_bytecode.py's C-10 shape - purely descriptive, never changes status.

findingLifecycleResult.description: M2. Output of compute_finding_lifecycle() / CLI mode 'finding-lifecycle'. Reuses diff_reports.py's diff_reports()/stableKey unchanged for every consecutive pair of scans.

businessRules: R-M1: M1/M2 results are structural facts, never automatic security verdicts - a bytecode/proxy change or a finding's new/resolved/regressed status may be entirely legitimate; interpreting significance is the analysis step's (or a human's) job.

R-M2: coverageStatus's NOT_ASSESSED is a monitoring-window/coverage status ONLY. compare_bytecode.py's five verdicts (MATCH/MISMATCH/UNAVAILABLE/INCOMPLETE/UNRESOLVED) are a completely separate, unmodified vocabulary - this script never adds a sixth bytecode verdict.

R-M3: A NOT_ASSESSED window, an empty flagChanges/proxyDrift list, or a currentStatus of 'resolved' is NEVER proof of safety - it only describes what this specific comparison, given the specific data it received, could determine.

R-M4: snapshotTimestamp (on every snapshot and every scan) is REQUIRED and always caller-supplied; this script never calls a clock. Snapshot/scan chronology is asserted by the caller's argument/array order, never inferred by parsing timestamp values.
R-M5: This script has no database, no cron/scheduling, no alerting, and no RPC/network calls - persisting history and acting on a reported change are entirely the calling workflow's responsibility.

R-M6: compute_temporal_snapshot_drift requires both snapshots to share the SAME (chainId, address) identity - chainId resolved to its canonical numeric form via chains.py (a name/alias is never identity by itself) and address normalized - a same-address-different-chain or same-chain-different-address pair, or one with an unresolvable chainId on either side, is always rejected before any comparison is attempted (D-064).
R-M7: adminAddress/ownerAddress drift is only reported when BOTH snapshots explicitly supply a value for that field - absence on either side is never guessed or treated as 'unchanged'.

R-M8: compute_finding_lifecycle reuses diff_reports.diff_reports()/score.compute_stable_key unchanged; a resolved finding that reappears in a later scan is tagged 'regressed', never silently re-reported as merely 'new'.
